Jon H: FYI new hire hit a weird combo: Windows + Python 3.12 (python.org) + venv -> SDK requests failing TLS verify. Same repo works on linux.
Priya M: Any error text?
Jon H: Short: `requests.exceptions.SSLError: [SSL: CERTIFICATE_VERIFY_FAILED] unable to get local issuer certificate` during client init.
Luis R: 3.12 changes SSL backend behavior in some windows builds; wheels might include openssl that doesn't consult OS cert store. Did they try certifi?
Jon H: Yep. Installing certifi and setting SSL_CERT_FILE to certifi.where() fixed it locally. But the onboarding script doesn't mention this and it's confusing for new hires.
Priya M: Two actions: 1) docs quickstart note for Windows+venv recommending certifi/SSL_CERT_FILE and how to pass ssl.SSLContext to client, 2) SDK change to accept ssl_context on AsyncClient and prefer SSL_CERT_FILE -> certifi -> system.
Luis R: Also watch typing — adding ssl_context param to AsyncClient needs updating typeshed/py.typed and async stubs so mypy doesn't complain in user code. I'll draft the PR and include unit tests that exercise both sync/async paths on Windows CI runner.
Jon H: Nice. Can docs-bot make a short onboarding tip we can add to the repo's README?
docs-bot: Created DOCS-511: "Quickstart: Windows venv TLS hint (certifi / ssl_context)" - https://redwood.atlassian.net/browse/DOCS-511
Priya M: Thanks. Leave thread until PR + docs merged so QE can validate across py3.8-3.12.
Jon H: Marking INF ticket with repro steps and sample script. Will ping when new wheel available. :thumbsup:
